turns.question: I'm starting to think seriously about retiring but I honestly don't know where to begin. What should I be thinking about?
turns.answer:
You can retire now under Article 11’s age-and-service rules. Section 11-130 applies to an employee age 55 or older but under 60 who has at least 10 years of service. It provides a full age-and-service annuity for an employee with 20 or more years of service. [40 ILCS 5/11-130]

The estimate is **$32,126.78 per year ($2,677.23 per month)** under Section 11-134.

**What I assumed:** the date you stop working is today, **September 13, 2026**.

That estimate is based on **21.5 years of service** and a highest average annual salary of **$69,956.40**. Your actual service credit depends on the Code’s service rules, including the treatment of duties performed, paid leave, certain unpaid leave, disability periods, and the exclusion of overtime or extra service. [40 ILCS 5/11-215]

Section 11-129 is the provision for withdrawal at age 60 or older but before 65, so it does not apply to retiring at age 56. Section 11-131 addresses withdrawal before age 55, so it also does not apply. Section 11-164 concerns refunds rather than the age-and-service annuity available here. [40 ILCS 5/11-129] [40 ILCS 5/11-131] [40 ILCS 5/11-164]

cases.name: A survivor question that uses none of the survivor vocabulary

turns.question: My wife is worried about what happens to her if something happens to me. What would she get?
turns.answer:
If you die while you are still working and before age 65, your wife would generally be entitled to a **widow’s annuity**. It would be calculated as of the date of your death from the amounts credited for your age-and-service annuity and widow’s annuity, plus applicable prior-service credits. The statute also limits the portion funded by city contributions. [40 ILCS 5/11-139]

The annuity means equal monthly payments for life, unless ended earlier under provisions that were not available here to review. [40 ILCS 5/11-124] Payments begin under the calendar-month rules in Section 11-124.

If you have eligible unmarried children, a child’s annuity may also be payable after your death until the child reaches age 18 or marries, whichever comes first, subject to the statutory conditions. [40 ILCS 5/11-153] Any remaining employee contributions may be paid to a beneficiary you designated in writing; if there is no surviving designated beneficiary, the statute provides for payment to your children or estate in the circumstances it describes. [40 ILCS 5/11-166]

No dollar amount can be stated from the information available. The amount turns on the accumulated annuity credits, applicable prior-service credits, and the statutory calculation as of your death. The provisions addressing termination on remarriage, certain annuity-payment rules, and the related termination provisions could not be established from the text available. Section 11-148.1 confirms that the survivor provisions apply equally to a surviving spouse of a female employee. [40 ILCS 5/11-148.1]

turns.answer:
Your pension annuity is not made tax-free by Article 11. The sections reviewed do not answer the federal or Illinois tax treatment, so I cannot establish from the Pension Code whether, or how much, would be taxable. [40 ILCS 5/11-223]

Health insurance is not guaranteed solely because you are an Article 11 member.
